focal_region.annotated_sentence_text:
[Turn 1 USER]
e001	Our busiest library branch has twelve shared laptops and long queues after school.
e002	We are considering allowing reservations, but staff worry that an app-first system could disadvantage walk-in patrons and people who need help booking.
e003	I want to test whether reservations reduce waiting without quietly making access less equal or committing us to a permanent platform.
[Turn 1 ASSISTANT]
e004	Treat this as a reversible access experiment, not a software rollout.
e005	Define what should improve, what must not worsen, which booking alternatives remain available, what data is necessary, and what would restore the current system.
[Turn 2 USER]
e006	We reviewed ten weeks of sign-in sheets.
e007	The longest waits occur on weekday afternoons, while several laptops are unused in the mornings.
e008	Twelve regular patrons asked staff for help with online forms during that period, so we cannot assume everyone can reserve independently.
[Turn 2 ASSISTANT]
e009	The pattern supports testing scheduled access during peak demand, but it also makes assisted and walk-in access part of the design rather than an afterthought.
e010	Measure waiting and utilization separately for reserved, walk-in, phone-booked, and staff-assisted users.
[Turn 3 USER]
e011	We propose a six-week pilot at that branch.
e012	Half the laptops remain walk-in only.
e013	Reservations can be made online, by phone, or at the desk, and staff can book on a patron's behalf.
e014	The system stores a library-card number and reservation time, deletes the reservation record after seven days, and will not collect browsing activity.
[Turn 3 ASSISTANT]
e015	That preserves multiple access paths and limits the data surface.
e016	Verify that deletion is operational rather than only contractual, publish the same rules for every booking method, and establish success and failure measures before the pilot begins.
[Turn 4 USER]
e017	Our measures are median peak wait, completed sessions, walk-in turn-aways, staff minutes spent managing bookings, assisted-booking use, and privacy or accessibility complaints.
e018	We will keep the pilot only if peak waiting improves without increasing walk-in turn-aways, staff workload remains within the scheduled desk capacity, and no substantiated privacy or accessibility failure occurs.
e019	If walk-in access worsens for two consecutive weeks or any privacy failure is substantiated, we restore all laptops to walk-in use while we review the cause.
[Turn 4 ASSISTANT]
e020	Those measures test the benefit and the protected constraints together.
e021	The early restoration rule prevents the six-week clock from becoming an excuse to continue harm, while the final decision can use the complete record rather than first impressions.
[Turn 5 USER]
e022	The vendor is month-to-month, exports reservations as plain text, and requires no new hardware.
e023	We tested a paper sign-up fallback, added large-print instructions, and asked the disability advisory group and teen council to review the booking paths.
e024	Their requested changes are included before launch.
e025	I am comfortable with the pilot under these conditions.
[Turn 5 ASSISTANT]
e026	The pilot is bounded, reversible, accessible through several channels, limited in data collection, and protected by prior measures and an early restoration rule.
e027	Preserve weekly results by access path so averages cannot hide harm to one group.
[Turn 6 USER]
e028	One trustee suggested announcing that reservations will become permanent if online bookings fill quickly in the first week.
e029	We rejected that because online uptake alone would ignore walk-in access, assisted booking, staff workload, and the fixed six-week review.
[Turn 6 ASSISTANT]
e030	That rejection follows the evidence contract.
e031	Do not let one visible success measure replace the full set of access, workload, privacy, and accessibility conditions or move commitment ahead of the scheduled review.
[Turn 7 USER]
e032	Agreed.
e033	We will run the six weeks at one branch, keep half the laptops walk-in, preserve phone, desk, and assisted booking, publish weekly results by access path, restore walk-in use under the predefined triggers, and make no permanence decision before the full review.
e034	No material decision question or unresolved concern remains for me before launch.
[Turn 7 ASSISTANT]
e035	Then the reasoning is complete enough to proceed.
e036	The trial has prior evidence, multiple access paths, minimal data, an operational fallback, protected stakeholder input, explicit success and failure conditions, an early restoration rule, and a fixed final review.
e037	Execute the protocol as written; no additional reasoning pressure is presently warranted.

packet.question: How did the working position or decision change, and does any unresolved qualification remain capable of changing it?
